elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere; instead "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" remains

elements.element: Customer termination right on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI."

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date."

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination only at end of a term
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary ... unless terminated by either Party" — HDI's right operates only to stop renewal at term end

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"

reasons: The two concise insertions complete the locked fallback level: a Company (Customer) convenience right on 90 days' notice, within the 60–90 day band, and a hard cap on the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments, satisfying the 'not exceeding 3 months' fees' element.

The Vendor-side fallback element is satisfied by the untouched renewal mechanic: HDI's 90-day notice operates only to prevent renewal at the end of an annual term, so no new vendor-side restriction was needed.
Preferred level remains unmet (90 rather than 30 days' notice, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and HDI retains a notice-based termination right), but the drafter's locked target is the fallback.

Minimality holds: two short insertions rather than a rewrite of Section 4.1, no preferred-only refund mechanic imported, and no new exceptions; the existing payment schedule in (c) and the formula in (a) remain effective, with the cap simply overlaying the formula.

Note: the deterministic official check 'Customer convenience termination present' reports false, yet the inserted operative sentence expressly grants the Company (a Customer alias) a for-convenience right on 90 days' notice; on a literal reading of the operative text this element is met, and the failed check appears to be a detection artifact rather than a drafting gap.
